title: Allocation tradeoffs - 1:1 roadmap and prep
body:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for 1:1 with Alex (capacity lead) — focus on short-term commit negotiation and autoscale tuning for S-revenue accounts.
- Goal: agree on a compact set of levers we can push in the next 14 days to reduce 95th-percentile token cost while keeping tail latency SLO intact.

Summary snapshot (current state):
- Committed pool: 240 A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved across us-west-2/us-east-1).
- Average sustained utilization (last 14d): 68%. 95th-percentile utilization: 92%.
- Allocated to high-priority tenants (reserved): 160 GPUs. Shared burstable pool: 80 GPUs.
- Observable pain: nightly ML batch warmups cause 20–30% bump at 02:00–04:00 UTC for hosted customers; dedicated tenants see increased queueing on long-context workloads.

Key assumptions for forecast window (next 60 days):
1) Two midsize S-tier customers plan to increase production requests by ~30% starting in 3 weeks (sales signal).
2) Model mix shift: ~15% traffic migrating to long-context (8k+) quantized variants.
3) Autoscale cooldown currently 10m, min-instance safety buffer = 10% of committed.

Primary tradeoffs to discuss (talking points):
- Conservative: increase reserved commit by 24 GPUs (1 rack) to keep headroom; cost impact vs. risk of throttling during forecasted ramp.
- Aggressive: keep commit flat, tune autoscale to rely on burst policy + regional spillover; risk: short latency spikes and higher per-token cost from on-demand hardware.
- Hybrid: allocate a short-term cross-region burst credit (software limit) + reduce cooldown to 5m + enable prefix caching warmup for long-context ramp windows.

Specific autoscale levers to recommend:
- Cooldown: 10m -> 5m during business hours for priority routes (owner: SRE/Tom).
- Min-instance safety buffer: 10% -> 6% for non-enterprise tenants; keep 12% for enterprise with SLAs.
- Burst window policy: enable 30-minute soft burst tokens that bypass strict quota checks but track accounting to finance.
- Pre-warm hooks: add KV-cache warmup trigger tied to job-schedules and model-rollout webhooks (owner: runtime team / Priya).

Numbers I want on the call (ask Alex to have these ready):
- Per-route 95th latency pre- and post-burst over last 7 days.
- Real-time committed vs. effective capacity by region (GPU-equivalent).
- Top 10 tenants by tail-usage in the last 30 days and whether they are on dedicated pools.

Draft negotiation framing for Sales/Finance (two short options):
- "Short buffer add": Ask for a 30-day trial of +24 GPUs with monthly true-up; frame as safety-first and bill only for committed if >14 days sustained.
- "Software credit": Offer region-bound burst credits (soft allocation) for 60 days with overage billing if sustained >2 weeks.

Open questions to resolve in 1:1:
- Can we scope a 30-day burst-credit ledger in billing design this sprint? (Billing owner: Kunal)
- Is reduced cooldown acceptable for enterprise tenants from a stability and cost forecasting POV?
- Do we have a quick signal to identify long-context traffic spikes before they hit the 95th percentile?

Meeting agenda (30 min suggested):
1) 5m — Quick situational: summarize snapshot + sales signals.
2) 10m — Walk through tradeoffs & autoscale levers with cost delta sketches.
3) 8m — Decide immediate action (commit increase vs hybrid).
4) 5m — Assign owners, timeline, and verify messaging to Sales/Finance.

Draft action items (post-call follow ups) — include owner and rough ETA: 
- A: Run a short simulation: project utilization with +24 GPUs vs. no commit change (owner: capacity-analytics / Diego) — ETA: 48 hours.
- B: Prototype reduced cooldown on staging for priority routes, monitor 5m/10m comparison (owner: SRE / Tom) — ETA: 72 hours.
- C: Draft Sales note outlining short-buffer offer and billing hook for 30-day trial (owner: revenue-ops / Priya) — ETA: 24 hours.
- D: Implement a KV-cache warmup experiment for one long-context tenant during nightly job window (owner: runtime / Priya) — ETA: 7 days.
- E: Add burst-credit accounting flag in billing backlog and scoped ticket (owner: billing / Kunal) — ETA: triage meeting next week.

Risk log (quick):
- If commit added and ramp delays > 30 days, we pay for idle hardware — mitigation: contract clause for credit/backout.
- If rely on on-demand burst and traffic patterns persist, may see 25–40% higher per-token cost for long-context models.
- Reduced cooldown could cause oscillation during noisy short bursts — mitigation: enable rate-limited scale-down and per-route hysteresis.

Prep checklist for me before 1:1:
- Pull the last 14d per-route utilization and attach small chart snippets.
- Confirm sales signal details for the two customers (expected start date, model mix).
- Prepare one-slide cost-delta mock with 3 scenarios (conservative/hybrid/aggressive).
- Add short script to demo prefix cache warmup (CLI steps) in case Alex asks for concrete ops steps.

Notes to self (one-liners):
- Keep tone collaborative, frame asks as temporary safety measures.
- Prioritize measurable experiments over immediate long-term commits unless sales provides signed leads.
- If we choose hybrid, ensure burst-accounting is tracked daily for finance visibility.

End of doc.
